analysis: The supplied units are base-side excerpts (lines 1587-3093) of landing/package-lock.json, a lockfile for the marketing landing site. They are not part of the provider, coordinator WebSocket, attestation, cache, fan-helper or add-on socket surfaces in the threat model. The patch excerpt is truncated (patch_excerpt_complete=false) but range_map_complete=true. It shows next 16.2.6 to 16.4.1 and a sharp / @img/sharp-libvips bump (0.34.5 to 0.35.5, 1.2.4 to 1.3.4) with the node engines floor raised to >=20.9.0. Changes in the base excerpt shown are limited to the ranges around 2421 (fast-uri), 3151-3225 and 3533-3603, which are outside the displayed base text or are not visible here. The displayed base excerpt has no head-side lines, so I could not cite or verify head content beyond the patch hunks. Resolved URLs in the visible patch point at registry.npmjs.org with sha512 integrity values, so there is no sign of a git, http or alternate-registry source in the visible portion. Nothing visible touches A-001..A-018 or TB-002/TB-003/TB-007/TB-009/TB-011/TB-012, and the landing site is not in the scoped provider threat model. Remaining unverified items: the truncated remainder of the patch (the changed ranges 626-1371 and 1599-1662 on the head side, 3310-3384, 3692-3738, 4028-4030) has not been inspected for resolved-URL or integrity anomalies, such as new install scripts, non-npm sources or unexpected new packages. A reviewer with the full lockfile diff should confirm those, though no specific risk is evident. The Next.js engine requirement of Node >=20.9.0 could affect build and deploy environments, which is an operational, not security, matter.
